text:
The Sabres' week had a jolt in it. Ryan McLeod sat as a healthy scratch Friday, and The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn framed it as a bit of a wake-up call for the whole room. Buffalo then beat Columbus 5-2, and Joe Yerdon of Bleacher Report reported the lines unchanged at Saturday's practice, McLeod still out, ahead of Vegas.

At 8-5-3, Buffalo is the definition of even. It has taken 49.98% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against) and scored 3.14 fewer goals than those chances deserved. A 42% playoff chance reflects a team that is neither good enough nor bad enough to stand out yet.

The best argument for more is one line. Jack Quinn, Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson have controlled 66% of the expected goals and outscored teams 8-2. Tage Thompson's group with Peyton Krebs and Benson has gone 7-0 in goals on a much thinner share, which won't hold.

In net, Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen is better than his save rate: 3.7 goals saved above expected over five starts. If the shooters catch up to the chances, this team climbs.
headline: Sabres keep it even, and kept a lesson
